title: HoloLedger: per-model & per-route performance strip + microchart spec
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: Design a compact, scan-first performance strip ("HoloLedger") that surfaces per-model and per-route health signals in a single horizontal row that can scale in lists. The strip is intended for the Redwood Console's endpoints table, model catalog list, and rollout panels. It must convey latency percentiles, throughput, token composition, cache efficiency, and unit-cost signals at a glance, with affordances to expand into a lightweight micro-dashboard. Scope: chart specs and interaction patterns for the strip and the expanded microcard. Non-goals: full-page telemetry workspace (separate existing effort), detailed trace timelines beyond a 5-span summary, long-form billing reports. Constraints: target rendering with lightweight canvas/SVG (must work at ~60fps when 200 rows render), support for streaming updates, accessible color tokens, and clear degrade paths when metric streams are delayed.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype with strip + expanded microcard interactions (hover, keyboard focus, click-to-pin) delivered
Spec'd microchart types: percentile-mini-bar, throughput-sparkline, token-composition mini-donut, cache-hit microline, cost-per-token microgauge
Edge case rules: missing data shown as dimmed 'no-sample' state; stale data >2m shows amber staleness pill
Handoff doc includes data shape examples (sample rate, percentile buckets, timestamp alignment) and rendering budgets (max 8pts per sec per row)
Contrast and color tokens meet WCAG 2.1 AA for normal text and are usable for color-blind palettes
comments: 2025-02-11 - Ava Patel: Initial pitch in design sync. Aim is to reduce per-route noise while keeping high fidelity for SRE/PM quick triage.
2025-02-12 - Jordan Lee: Eng note - need explicit data contract for P50/P95/P99, and a streaming fallback if percentile aggregation is delayed by >3s.
2025-02-14 - Miguel Santos (PM): Review: prioritize latency tail and KV cache hit as first-class signals for Dedicated customers. Add a low-cost indicator for quantized serving variants.
2025-02-15 - Design review: swap mini-donut to stacked microbars for token composition to avoid small-slices legibility issues. Decision logged in Confluence.
2025-02-17 - Accessibility review: adjusted hues for color-blind palette; ensured focus states are 3px outline and keyboard-expand is supported.
2025-02-18 - Jordan Lee: Updated spec clarifies rendering budgets and adds fallback text for stale streams. Ready for engineering sizing.
Open: Confirm rollout overlay interaction with canary traffic splits (PM / Eng to decide how percent overlay is derived).
design_notes: Visual language: minimal chrome, 28px strip height (collapsed), expanded microcard 320x280. Microcharts should prioritize small-multiples readability: - Latency: three skinny bars (P50/P95/P99) with hover tooltip showing sample count. - Throughput: 60s sparkline with per-second bars aggregated to 1s. - Token Composition: 3-segment stacked microbar (prompt/inference/system) with percentage labels on hover. - Cache-efficiency: 1-line microline with dot for last-known hit-rate. - Cost-per-token: tiny radial microgauge with green/amber/red thresholds tied to tier settings. Interactions: hover to expand to microcard, keyboard focus to open details, click to pin. Performance: virtualize rendering for lists >50 rows; prefer canvas-backend for sparkline to reduce DOM nodes.
implementation_guidance: Data contract: timestamp (ISO8601), route_key, model_key, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, throughput_rps, tokens_in_prompt, tokens_in_completion, kv_cache_hit_rate (0-1), cost_per_1000_tokens_usd, sample_count, last_updated. UI should sample and smooth short-term spikes with EWMA alpha=0.3 for display, raw values remain available in tooltip. For canary overlays include optional field 'traffic_split_pct'.
